editorial: You follow Joe from the start as her story moves into darker adult years, with Seligman listening and reacting to every detail. The film keeps the same talk-heavy style, but the mood gets heavier and more uncomfortable. It is not a light watch, yet it stays strangely gripping because you want to understand how Joe ended up where she is. The cast commits fully, and the story pushes into risky territory without losing its strange, dry humor. The acting is really strong, especially in the emotional scenes, and the pacing keeps you moving through tough material without feeling slow. Still, the explicit content and bleak choices will turn many viewers away, so this is best for adults who can handle very intense drama. If you are curious, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Joe finishes her story and Seligman reveals he has never had sex. He then tries to force himself on her, breaking the trust built during their long talk. Joe reacts by shooting him and leaving his apartment. The twist is that the man who seemed kind and understanding becomes another threat, showing Joe's world stays dangerous and she must keep protecting herself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves intense adult drama and character studies.
